questions.question: In computer architecture and memory management, what is the primary role of a Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB)?
options: It caches recently used virtual-to-physical address translations to accelerate memory accesses by avoiding multi-level page table walks in main memory.
It dynamically reorders memory loads and stores to optimize row buffer hit rates in the off-chip DRAM controller.
It monitors and resolves coherence conflicts between L1 data caches in a multi-core symmetric multiprocessing system.
It dynamically translates architectural register specifiers into physical register IDs during the instruction decode stage.
It buffers prefetched instructions to prevent instruction cache starvation during branch misprediction recovery.

questions.question: In deep-submicron ASIC physical design and fabrication, what is the 'antenna effect' (plasma-induced gate oxide damage), and how is it standardly mitigated during physical layout?
options: High-frequency electromagnetic emissions radiating from global clock nets; mitigated by surrounding sensitive nets with grounded shield wires.

Electrostatic charge accumulation on long conductive interconnects during plasma etching that can tunnel through and rupture thin gate oxide; mitigated by inserting antenna diodes or routing jumpers to higher metal layers.
Parasitic LC resonance across power delivery stripes causing localized supply collapse; mitigated by spreading decoupling capacitor cells along standard-cell rows.
Capacitive crosstalk between high-speed adjacent signal wires leading to signal integrity glitches; mitigated by increasing wire spacing and driver sizing.
Thermal stress migration in copper interconnects under high operational current density; mitigated by widening metal traces and doubling contact vias.

questions.question: In hierarchical cache subsystem design, what is the primary architectural advantage of enforcing a strictly 'Inclusive' multi-level cache policy (e.g., L2 is strictly inclusive of L1)?
options: It maximizes the aggregate storage capacity across all cache levels by ensuring that no data block is ever replicated between L1 and L2.
It guarantees that an eviction of a modified cache block in L1 automatically purges the line from L2 without requiring a writeback.

External cache coherence snoops and invalidation requests only need to query the outer inclusive cache (L2); if a line is missing there, it is guaranteed not to reside in L1, eliminating unnecessary L1 lookups.
It allows write misses in L1 to completely bypass L2 and directly update system memory without allocating space in intermediate levels.
It eliminates all capacity and conflict misses in the cache hierarchy by dynamically resizing cache ways according to workload demand.

questions.question: In Static Timing Analysis (STA) under On-Chip Variation (OCV) derating, what is the fundamental purpose of Clock Reconvergence Pessimism Removal (CRPR), also known as Common Path Pessimism Removal (CPPR)?
options: To compensate for setup-time degradation caused by dynamic supply voltage droop occurring along high-activity data paths.
To calculate and eliminate high-frequency phase jitter introduced by the on-chip Phase-Locked Loop (PLL).
To model the latency difference between rising and falling transitions along combinational logic trees.
To remove artificial timing pessimism introduced when differing min/max OCV derating factors are applied to the shared physical segments of the clock tree for the launch and capture paths.
To remove the propagation delay penalties associated with through-silicon vias (TSVs) in multi-die 2.5D/3D packaging.

questions.question: In asynchronous and combinational digital circuit design, what causes a static-1 hazard, and how is it fundamentally eliminated in two-level Sum-of-Products (SOP) logic?
options: Excessive output capacitive loading that slows the output rise time below the clock period; eliminated by inserting balanced buffer trees.
Clock skew exceeding the flip-flop propagation delay in sequential loops; eliminated by inserting delay buffers on the clock capture path.
Charge sharing at intermediate floating nodes in dynamic CMOS gates; eliminated by adding a weak PMOS keeper transistor.
Capacitive cross-coupling between adjacent routing tracks causing transient voltage glitches; eliminated by inserting shielding wires tied to VDD.

Unequal propagation delays along converging paths causing the output to momentarily dip to 0 during an input transition between adjacent 1-cells in a Karnaugh map; eliminated by adding a redundant consensus product term that bridges the adjacent prime implicants.
